sections.content:
You know *ponerse a* + infinitive from A2 Unit 32 (*se puso a llover*, *me puse a limpiar la casa*). It is the most flexible of the "start" phrases, so this lesson recaps it and adds only one thing: how it differs from *echarse a*, which you met in the last lesson.

*Ponerse a* works with a planned task (*se puso a trabajar*), with a sudden reaction (*se puso a llorar*) and with weather (*se puso a nevar*). *Echarse a* works only with the reaction.

sections.title: Which verb fits?
rows: Después de cenar, me puse a escribir el informe.
A planned task: only ponerse a works.
Al ver la foto, se puso a llorar. / Al ver la foto, se echó a llorar.
A sudden reaction: both work; echarse a sounds more sudden.
De repente se puso a nevar.
Weather: ponerse a works; echarse a is not used.
Los técnicos se pusieron a revisar el motor.
A job that people choose to start: only ponerse a works.

sections.content: Do not mix up *ponerse a* + infinitive with *ponerse* + adjective. You know *ponerse* + adjective from B2 Unit 22: *Se puso triste* means she became sad, but *Se puso a llorar* means she started to cry. The little word *a* and an infinitive after it make the difference.
